name: Annadhana Mandapam (TDB Free Sadya, Sannidhanam)
signature_dish: Free Kerala sadya served to pilgrims round the clock — the largest such hall in India
why_it_matters: The free-meal hall run by the Travancore Devaswom Board behind the Malikappuram Temple at Sannidhanam — the biggest annadanam facility in India, equipped to feed more than two lakh pilgrims a day round the clock. In 2025 the TDB upgraded the menu from pulao-and-sambar to a full Kerala sadya. For most Sabarimala pilgrims this is the meal of the pilgrimage.
insider_tip: The meal is entirely free — breakfast, lunch and dinner are served every day the temple is open, including monthly pujas. Sabarimala is a seasonal pilgrim shrine (busiest in the Mandala-Makaravilakku season, mid-November to mid-January); plan around the temple calendar.
signature_address: Annadhana Mandapam, Sannidhanam, Sabarimala, Pathanamthitta, Kerala 689713

name: Aravana & Appam Prasadam Counters (TDB, Sannidhanam)
signature_dish: Aravana — the jaggery-rice payasam prasadam — and sweet appam
why_it_matters: The Travancore Devaswom Board prasadam counters at Sannidhanam, near the Pathinettampadi (the 18 holy steps), sell aravana — the famous jaggery-and-rice payasam — and sweet appam that pilgrims carry home. The TDB runs labs at Sannidhanam and Pampa to test the safety and quality of the appam and aravana and their raw materials.
insider_tip: Aravana cans and appam packets are the prasadam every Sabarimala pilgrim carries back. Buy from the official TDB counters at Sannidhanam, not informal vendors, to be sure of quality. This is take-home prasadam rather than a sit-down eatery.
signature_address: TDB Prasadam Counters, near Pathinettampadi, Sannidhanam, Sabarimala, Pathanamthitta, Kerala 689713

name: Nilackal Annadanam & Pilgrim Canteen
signature_dish: Free and low-cost vegetarian meals at the Nilackal base before the trek to Pampa
why_it_matters: Nilackal is the main vehicle base for the Sabarimala pilgrimage, where pilgrims transfer to shuttle buses for Pampa. The Travancore Devaswom Board has allocated a building here to the Sabarimala Ayyappa Seva Samajam to run annadanam and pilgrim services — free and low-cost vegetarian food at the start of the route.
insider_tip: A practical meal stop at the Nilackal base before the onward leg to Pampa and the trek up. Strictly vegetarian, in keeping with pilgrims' 41-day austerity. Busiest in the Mandala-Makaravilakku season; quiet otherwise as the shrine is seasonal.
signature_address: Nilackal Base, KSRTC Terminal, Sabarimala route, Pathanamthitta, Kerala 689711
